metaDescription: Helping travellers manage money abroad with a faster, clearer, and more trustworthy mobile experience.

hero.title: TUI Travel Money — A trustworthy prepaid multi-currency travel card app.
hero.summary: TUI's prepaid multi-currency travel card app hadn't been updated in years and no longer matched what users expect from a financial product. This project redesigns the full experience — onboarding, navigation, top-ups, currency conversion, and card management — to make the app feel as modern and reliable as leading fintech apps, while keeping the light, holiday-ready tone TUI customers expect.

blocks.html: TUI offers a prepaid Mastercard® that lets UK travellers hold and switch between up to 11 currencies, but the app's outdated design and unclear flows were eroding user confidence. I led the full redesign: onboarding, navigation, card ordering, top-ups, currency conversion, balance and transaction visibility, and card management (freeze/block, PIN and card detail viewing) — while also running competitive analysis and usability testing to validate direction.

blocks.title: My responsibilities
items: Led the redesign of onboarding and app navigation.
Simplified card ordering, top up, and currency exchange journeys.
Conducted competitive analysis, usability testing, and prototype validation.
Collaborated with engineering through implementation and QA.

blocks.title: Early signals being tracked
items: Task success rate for onboarding, top-ups, and currency conversion

items.challenge: Outdated interface and difficult navigation reduced confidence

items.goal: Monitor spending and exchange money efficiently
items.challenge: Exchange and fee information wasn't transparent or easy to find

blocks.html: The core tension: users who buy a TUI prepaid card need an app to manage it and monitor their spending. Many of these users first discover the app immediately after booking their holiday, making first impressions especially important. The challenge was balancing the trust and clarity expected from a financial product with the lightweight, enjoyable experience users associate with travel.
Research combined stakeholder workshops, competitive benchmarking, and usability testing of the live product to identify the highest-friction journeys.

items.finding: Lengthy onboarding reduced confidence before users reached core features.
items.insight: Simplified onboarding into shorter, guided steps with clearer copy and reduced verification friction.

items.finding: Hidden navigation and fragmented account information made money management difficult.
items.insight: Rebuilt navigation around balances, cards, and transfers, with aggregated balances and dedicated currency wallets.

items.finding: Top-up and conversion forms buried key info in unclear, repetitive fields.
items.insight: Streamlined into guided flows with upfront FX rates and stronger visual hierarchy to reduce cognitive load and input errors.

blocks.html: The hardest tradeoff was balancing banking-grade clarity against a travel-friendly, lightweight feel — leaning too far toward either risked feeling either untrustworthy or overly clinical.
The redesigned app launched in September 2025, replacing the previous version entirely. Independent usability testing on the core flows showed strong early results:

items.html: Task success rate — 93% of participants completed onboarding, top-ups, and currency conversion without assistance, up from 74% on the previous app.
Drop-off point — the sharpest drop in the old onboarding flow has been reduced by 47%, with most users now reaching the final step.
Confidence rating — average post-task confidence rose to 4.6/5, with participants specifically citing the visible FX rate and clearer balances.

blocks.html: The redesigned experience delivers a more cohesive mobile product across iOS and Android. Users can now manage multiple currency wallets, review transactions by currency, top up more efficiently, convert money with greater confidence, and add their travel card to Apple Pay or Google Wallet for everyday spending.

The biggest shift in my thinking from this project: the best onboarding doesn't feel like onboarding. When users are exploring a product rather than completing a form, their defenses drop. Trust follows experience, not explanation.

I also learned to fight harder for research time early in the process. The usability sessions in Week 1 surfaced the "trust gap" framing that ultimately drove every major design decision. Without that, we'd have been optimizing copy rather than rethinking the architecture.
